clue.text: Dodgy contract he shows private eye outfit?

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady contract reveals what a hired detective wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges the letters of CONTRACT HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The belted raincoat is the classic costume of the fictional private detective, hence the question mark.

clue.text: National Trust homes are investments, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of the last four words are taken

explanation.surface: A heritage charity declares that its properties are mainly investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Trust' reads as one name, the British heritage charity; 'National' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, and a citizen of Thailand is one example.

clue.text: City pro's sound return

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
a pro is a prostitute, slang ho; the 's is the possessive joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A professional from the City has a sound comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is sound bouncing back off a surface to the listener.

clue.text: Salon offers massage — no discretion!

indicators.note: to massage figures is to work them over, so these letters are manipulated into a new order

explanation.surface: A hair salon advertises massages but promises no privacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair products for softening hair after shampoo are items a hairdresser's salon sells and uses.

clue.text: Very loudly filling money boxes

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: coins are money
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Money boxes are being filled noisily with coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money boxes' looks like one thing; 'boxes' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Burial caskets are the boxes that hold the dead.

clue.text: Requited — adult volume by English journalist

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An adult book by an English journalist was repaid in kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite a wrong is to pay it back, which is taking revenge for it.

clue.text: Opening of Trump's border for those people

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: Trump opens his border to certain people.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural pronoun stands for a group of others, those people over there.

clue.text: Irregular success with young lady

parts.note: a hit is a success
and means with, joining things
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone has had uneven luck romancing a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard succeeds some of the time and fails the rest, so it is uneven in quality.

clue.text: Store endlessly potent drug in dish

parts.note: a mine is a rich store, as in a mine of information

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

parts.note: potent means strong
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a powerful narcotic in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' docks the last letter of STRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian vegetable soup is served as a course, and a dish is a course of food.

clue.text: Pronouncement of a royal act leads to pedestrian complaint

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a gives A; a king is a royal; a feat is a notable act

explanation.surface: A royal proclamation brings complaints from people on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, A KING FEAT sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore soles are a typical grumble of someone who has been walking, a pedestrian.

clue.text: Way peacekeepers use tasers, for example

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
the UN sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: This is how peacekeeping troops deploy electric weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasers are electric weapons that daze or knock out a target, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Revealing fault if liar ends up wavering

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A liar's story starts to waver and gives the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue said to expose a hidden wish is an error that reveals the mind.

clue.text: Cocktail bar speciality that one might regret in the morning?

definitions.meaning: a cocktail bar is known for blending spirits into cocktails

definitions.text: that one might regret in the morning?
definitions.meaning: drinking several kinds of alcohol in one night is blamed for a bad hangover

explanation.surface: A bar's signature skill is also tomorrow's regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining spirits is what bartenders do, and also the drinker's mistake that brings a hangover.

clue.text: Crazy family is a recipe for disaster?

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin are family

explanation.surface: A mad family always ends in catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The slippery peel underfoot is the comedy cause of a fall, hence a recipe for trouble; the question mark flags the food pun.

clue.text: Even gossip is flattery

parts.note: smooth means even, level
talk is gossip

explanation.surface: Even idle chatter counts as buttering someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb; it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Slick, persuasive patter is a form of flattery used to win someone over.

clue.text: Indentations under the shoulder strap I'm adjusting

indicators.note: adjusting means altering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts a shoulder strap that is digging in.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollows beneath where the arm joins the body are the oxters, under the shoulder.

clue.text: Dutch stranger is one to beat

parts.note: rum means odd, so rummer means stranger

explanation.surface: An odder Dutchman is the rival everyone must overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is also the setter's name. RUM is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist is someone whose job is to beat the drums, not an opponent to defeat.

clue.text: Unlimited cash to cover rising quantities

indicators.note: to cover is to wrap around, so the pick goes round the other piece
unlimited means without its limits, the outer letters

parts.note: to mount is to rise, as prices mount

explanation.surface: Endless money is needed to cover soaring sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like it reverses something; here it is just the verb mount, as prices mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums or totals of something are measured quantities of it.

clue.text: One punching presenter of alternative facts would be more exciting

indicators.note: punching means making a hole into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Sean Spicer, Trump's press secretary, presented what were called alternative facts
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Assaulting Trump's spin doctor would liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Racier or hotter in flavour, so livelier and more stimulating.

clue.text: Colour seen in metallic rims once

indicators.note: seen in means sitting inside these words, spread across them

explanation.surface: A colour that used to be seen on metal wheel rims.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep purplish red is a colour.

clue.text: American welcome in Tory pad

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: CON, Conservative, is a Tory
hi is a greeting, a welcome

explanation.surface: An American is greeted in a Conservative's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' looks like slang for a home; it is the soft thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded pillow or soft rest is a pad.

clue.text: Utterly perplexed as she may be, he treats wind casually

definitions.text: Utterly perplexed as she may be

indicators.note: casually means in a careless, haphazard way, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman is baffled because her partner is so offhand about breaking wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' rearranges HE TREATS WIND; 'as she may be' explains the feminine pronoun in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely baffled and out of ideas, the idiom for someone who no longer knows what to do.

clue.text: Oddly missing seat in May's unstable summit

indicators.note: missing the odd letters, so only the even letters are kept

explanation.surface: Theresa May's shaky summit conference is short of seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly missing' drops the odd letters of SEAT IN MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is a peak that erupts, so its top is unstable.

clue.text: Short order could be part of smorgasbord

indicators.note: being part of the word means the letters lie inside it

explanation.surface: A short food order could come from a Swedish buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order against antisocial behaviour; 'Short' says it is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for anti-social behaviour order, a court order.

clue.text: Need to return small energy unit

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lack means need

explanation.surface: Someone needs to give back a little unit of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilocalorie, abbreviated, is a unit of food energy; 'small' signals the abbreviation.

clue.text: Bird I left behind has singular interests

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
late means behind time
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A bird the speaker left behind has its own peculiar interests.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse or excite someone's curiosity is to interest them; the verb form matches.

clue.text: Northern base harbouring our country's weapon

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: E is the base of natural logarithms
UK is the setter's country, the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A northern military base shelters Britain's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear bomb or missile is a weapon, informally.

clue.text: GP developed instrument

parts.note: G is short for grand and P for piano, so each letter developed into its full word

explanation.surface: A family doctor has created a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: GP looks like a general practitioner; G is the abbreviation for a grand (a thousand pounds) and P for piano (soft).
explanation.definitionFit: The large horizontal concert keyboard is a musical instrument.
